findings.title: Nothing tests that `unchanged` reaches the renderer and suppresses the toast
findings.body: The flag crosses three layers: `relocateWorkspace` sets it (pinned in `relocate.test.ts:158`), `relocateFolder` copies it into the IPC result (`index.ts:349`), and `onRelocated` skips the toast (`workspaces-context.tsx:168`). Only the first hop has a test. If the spread at `index.ts:349` were dropped, or the early return here removed, the "now points to the new folder" toast would come back for a no-op and every test would still pass. A small test in the workspaces context or dialog tests would cover it: resolve `relocate` with `{ ok: true, unchanged: true, workspace }` and assert no toast, then resolve it without the flag and assert the toast.

contracts.action: Picking the workspace's current folder in "Change folder…" returns `unchanged: true`, and the renderer shows no toast
contracts.equivalent_path: A real relocation (`relocateFolder` → `relocateWorkspace` → `registry.relocate`), which ends with `folderChanged` shown by `onRelocated`.
contracts.before_after: Before: the same-path early return gave `{ok:true, entry}` and the renderer showed "now points to the new folder" for a no-op. After: `relocate.ts:43-45` adds `unchanged: true`, `index.ts:349` forwards it, and `workspaces-context.tsx:168` returns before the toast. The probe, `refreshTitles` and `broadcastState` in `relocateFolder` (index.ts:342-345) still run, so a deleted identity.json is still rewritten.
contracts.visible_effect: The user picks the same folder and the dialog or Settings shows no message. The dialog's own handling of `result.ok` is unchanged (`workspace-dialog.tsx:145`).
contracts.failure_mode: No new async call. If the flag were lost, the old misleading toast would come back, and no test would catch it.

contracts.action: An offline edit of a `pendingInit` workspace now keeps `pendingInit` set
contracts.equivalent_path: The `availability` probe, which clears `pendingInit` when it writes the identity file (lines 743-749) or adopts one (line 725). `checkRelocate` accepts a folder with `.kaipu` and no identity only while `pendingInit` is set (line 855).
contracts.before_after: Before: any edit deleted `pendingInit`, so a later "Change folder…" to a moved drive with Kaipu items and no identity.json was refused as `has-items-no-identity`. After: it is deleted only when the identity was written to the folder (`savedToFolder`). The registry change is marked `pendingIdentity` (line 638) and the probe after the move writes the edited name and color under the registered id (lines 733-749), then clears all three flags.
contracts.visible_effect: The renamed workspace can be pointed at the remounted drive, and the new name carries over to the folder. The test at registry-relocate.test.ts:221-243 covers this.
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder already holds an identity with the registered id when the probe runs, the `pendingIdentity` branch (line 670) writes the identity but does not delete `pendingInit`. The next probe clears it through the `stale` check (line 702), so it is harmless and self-healing.

thread_replies.reply: Addressed. `relocate.ts:43-45` returns `unchanged: true`, `index.ts:349` forwards it, and `workspaces-context.tsx:168` skips the toast. The main-side flag is tested; the forwarding and the renderer skip are not (see the finding on `workspaces-context.tsx`).
Addressed. The same-path early return in `relocate.ts:42-45` skips `relocateActive`, and `relocate.test.ts:155-161` checks the log is empty and the generation is unchanged.

The part you fixed holds. `checkRelocate` accepts a `pendingInit` workspace's moved folder (`registry.ts:855`), and the offline edit no longer clears `pendingInit` (`registry.ts:634`). The new test at `registry-relocate.test.ts:221-243` covers it. The adopted-id case you deferred is not changed here.

input.summary: The change holds up. The `unchanged` flag is set in `relocate.ts:43-45` and forwarded at `index.ts:349`. The renderer skips the toast at `workspaces-context.tsx:168`. The `pendingInit` fix at `registry.ts:634` is consistent with `availability` and `checkRelocate`, and its test covers the real path. I found one gap: only the `relocate.ts` hop of the `unchanged` flag has a test. The IPC forwarding and the renderer skip are untested. The three open threads on these files are addressed.

findings.title: Nothing tests that `unchanged` reaches the renderer and suppresses the toast
findings.body: The flag crosses three layers: `relocateWorkspace` sets it (pinned in `relocate.test.ts:158`), `relocateFolder` copies it into the IPC result (`index.ts:349`), and `onRelocated` skips the toast (`workspaces-context.tsx:168`). Only the first hop has a test. If the spread at `index.ts:349` were dropped, or the early return here removed, the "now points to the new folder" toast would come back for a no-op and every test would still pass. A small test in the workspaces context or dialog tests would cover it: resolve `relocate` with `{ ok: true, unchanged: true, workspace }` and assert no toast, then resolve it without the flag and assert the toast.

contracts.action: Picking the workspace's current folder in "Change folder…" returns `unchanged: true`, and the renderer shows no toast
contracts.equivalent_path: A real relocation (`relocateFolder` → `relocateWorkspace` → `registry.relocate`), which ends with `folderChanged` shown by `onRelocated`.
contracts.before_after: Before: the same-path early return gave `{ok:true, entry}` and the renderer showed "now points to the new folder" for a no-op. After: `relocate.ts:43-45` adds `unchanged: true`, `index.ts:349` forwards it, and `workspaces-context.tsx:168` returns before the toast. The probe, `refreshTitles` and `broadcastState` in `relocateFolder` (index.ts:342-345) still run, so a deleted identity.json is still rewritten.
contracts.visible_effect: The user picks the same folder and the dialog or Settings shows no message. The dialog's own handling of `result.ok` is unchanged (`workspace-dialog.tsx:145`).
contracts.failure_mode: No new async call. If the flag were lost, the old misleading toast would come back, and no test would catch it.

contracts.action: An offline edit of a `pendingInit` workspace now keeps `pendingInit` set
contracts.equivalent_path: The `availability` probe, which clears `pendingInit` when it writes the identity file (lines 743-749) or adopts one (line 725). `checkRelocate` accepts a folder with `.kaipu` and no identity only while `pendingInit` is set (line 855).
contracts.before_after: Before: any edit deleted `pendingInit`, so a later "Change folder…" to a moved drive with Kaipu items and no identity.json was refused as `has-items-no-identity`. After: it is deleted only when the identity was written to the folder (`savedToFolder`). The registry change is marked `pendingIdentity` (line 638) and the probe after the move writes the edited name and color under the registered id (lines 733-749), then clears all three flags.
contracts.visible_effect: The renamed workspace can be pointed at the remounted drive, and the new name carries over to the folder. The test at registry-relocate.test.ts:221-243 covers this.
contracts.failure_mode: If the folder already holds an identity with the registered id when the probe runs, the `pendingIdentity` branch (line 670) writes the identity but does not delete `pendingInit`. The next probe clears it through the `stale` check (line 702), so it is harmless and self-healing.
